stem: Which feature of the paediatric airway most directly increases airway resistance compared with adults?

options.text: Lower proportion of foetal haemoglobin until 6 months

explanation: Smaller diameter airways are the correct answer. In infants and young children, a narrower airway increases resistance, so swelling or obstruction can cause rapid deterioration.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Page 28

rationale: Paediatric airway calibre is smaller than in adults, which increases resistance and helps explain why airway emergencies can escalate quickly.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because a smaller airway diameter markedly increases resistance to airflow.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because fewer, not more, alveoli are described in young children, and alveolar number does not directly increase airway resistance.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the source describes an increased proportion of foetal haemoglobin until 6 months, not a lower proportion.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because young children have a compliant chest wall, not a more rigid one.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the airway is smaller in diameter, not shorter and wider.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
